Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Ultraviolet Mapping Spectrometer (Alice)
record.mission_name: New Horizons Pluto Kuiper Belt Flyby
record.description: The Alice instrument is an ultraviolet mapping spectrometer designed to study the atmosphere of Pluto. The scientific objectives are to determine the mole fractions of N2, CH4, CO, and Ar to 1% in total mixing ratio in the atmosphere, to profile the temperature structure of the upper atmosphere, and to acheive H lyman-alpha mapping of the Pluto-Charon system to study the rate of Roche-lobe flow from Pluto to Charon. it will also be used to search for atmospheres around Charon and any Kuiper belt Objects encountered. Alice has two modes of operation, an airglow mode which measures emissions from from the atmosphere and an occultation mode which is used when the Sun or a bright star can be viewed through the atmosphere. Alice covers the wavelength range from 52-187 nanometers with a spectral resolution of 0.183 nm. The slit field of view is 1.7 x 70 milliradians with an angular resolution of 1.7 x 5.2 milliradians per pixel. The field of view through the solar occultation aperture is 35 x 35 milliradians. Along with the Ralph instrument, Alice is part of the The Pluto Exploration Remote Sensing Investigation (PERSI).
